author: mwc360
body:
This PR addresses correctness issues the core logic of Auto Compaction.

#### Which Delta project/connector is this regarding?
- [x] Spark
- [ ] Standalone
- [ ] Flink
- [ ] Kernel
- [ ] Other (fill in here)

## Description
- Resolves #4045 If DELTA_AUTO_COMPACT_MIN_FILE_SIZE was unset, it was defaulting to Long.MaxValue which resulted in large files counting torwards the minNumFiles threshold for AC to be triggered. This resulted in compaction running more frequently up to the point of running after every write as a table grows in size.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e3de6f4-48f5-4d83-b061-c12ec9a76fa0)
The below is the expected behavior on the same test suite as produced by Databricks: 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/055d432a-8cd5-42fb-9819-cbe6a7bcf89a)

- Resolves #4045 AC eval criteria incorrectly didn't always require enough small files and would trigger AC if AC wasn't run as part of the last operation. AC should only evaluate as `shouldCompact` if compaction wasn't just run AND there are enough small files.

- Resolves #4487 Files written from a prior session were not considered in evaluation. This means that AC can be trigger when too many small files are written in a single session. JVM restart resets the AutoCompactPartitionStats metrics. Since `fileSizeHistogram` in the checksum is supported now, we can use this to evaluate the number of small files for unpartitioned tables. For partitioned tables it falls back to existing AutoCompactPartitionStats code path.
 
## How was this patch tested?
- AutoCompactSuite.scala was updated to add more robust coverage to ensure large files don't trigger AC.
- I separately ran a test suite which runs 200 iterations of merging data into a Delta table and monitors for AC being triggered to ensure that compaction is running based on having small files >= minNumFiles. I also ran this same test suite in Databricks to ensure that the behavior matches.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing changes?
No.

cmd2/argparse_custom.py:1364:44: note: See https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html#incompatible-overrides
```

I tried replacing `typing.IO[str]` with `SupportsWrite[str]` as suggested, but then that broke things down the road because we need this thing to support an `isatty` method within `ansi.style_aware_write`. So for now we can just suppress this warning.
   ```

body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

While updating multiple fields, changes were being applied one by one. During this process, the system periodically polls the cluster for status updates. However, the cluster status was prematurely transitioning to active instead of updating. This led to:
- Some updates being reverted.
- Certain changes getting skipped intermittently.

To address this, we now ensure that while making updates, the cluster status is enqueued as updating. This keeps the cluster continuously checking for upstream changes and prevents unintended timeouts.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**
[Issue #667](https://github.com/rancher/aks-operator/issues/667)

body:
## 2.0.0

###
- Adds entitlements to subscriptions, allowing you to set them using:
  - `await Superwall.shared.setSubscriptionStatus(status)` by passing in one of:
    - `SubscriptionStatusActive(entitlements: entitlements))`
      - Note: Passing in empty entitlements will set the subscription status to inactive
    - `SubscriptionStatusInactive`
    - `SubscriptionStatusUnknown`
- Subscribing to subscription status updates via stream `Superwall.shared.subscriptionStatus`
- `SuperwallBuilder` which will automatically update the state whenever subscription status changes
- `Superwall.shared.registerEvent` has now been replaced with `Superwall.shared.registerPlacement`
- `handleSuperwallEvent(SuperwallEventInfo eventInfo)` has been replaced with `handleSuperwallPlacement(SuperwallPlacementInfo placementInfo)`
- `PaywallPresentationHandler.onDismiss` now has 2 arguments, `PaywallInfo` and `PaywallResult`

As suggested by @UlfNorell in https://github.com/agda/agda/issues/7693#issuecomment-2668463863

Refactors some operations on `Order` and removed the `Mat` constructor entirely to try and clean things up a bit. I am new to the Agda codebase so there is a high chance I have missed something important somewhere. It remains a little strange to me that `PartialOrd Order` implements a total ordering (in spite of the fact that we can't give a fully correct total ordering!)

Unfortunately, this PR still doesn't accept the motivating examples (hence I haven't added test cases yet). Scroll down for explanations.

Side note: what's the story with "(un)usable" decreases? The comment claims "no unusable decreases are generated by TermCheck", but there seems to have been some effort made to annotate `Decr`s of `<= 0`  as unusable (e.g. `le = Decr False 0`), but this feels a bit redundant given how easy it is to compare the decrease's value with `0`.
